The `cetra` binary runs the server (`cetra serve`), administers a data directory (`cetra admin`) and talks to a running server (`cetra login`, `cetra query`, `cetra traces`, `cetra projects`). This page is generated from the binary's `--help`.

## `cetra`

```text
LLM observability server

Usage: cetra <COMMAND>

Commands:
  serve     Start the HTTP server
  admin     Admin operations on this data directory (users, encryption key, deletions)
  version   Print the cetra version
  health    Exit 0 if the server answers `GET <url>/readyz` with 200 (the container healthcheck)
  login     Save a personal access token for a server
  logout    Revoke the saved personal access token
  query     Run a SQL query on a project
  traces    List and show traces
  projects  List the projects you can read
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

### `cetra serve`

```text
Start the HTTP server

Usage: cetra serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Overrides `CETRA_CONFIG`

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### `cetra admin`

```text
Admin operations on this data directory (users, encryption key, deletions)

Usage: cetra admin <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create-user            Create a user
  reset-password         Print a password reset URL
  list-users             List users
  rotate-encryption-key  Re-encrypt stored secrets under a new key. Stop the server first
  reapply-deletions      Re-open the deletions of another data directory that this one lacks (after a backup restore). Both `meta.db` files must be at this binary's schema; run `cetra admin migrate` on a restored older backup first
  backup                 Back up the running server into DIR (online; the server writes DIR)
  gc-orphans             Delete objects the catalog does not know and report the ones it misses. Stop the server first
  migrate                Migrate `meta.db` and `catalog.db` to this version's schema, then exit. Stop the server first
  entitlements           Org entitlements
  org-sso                An org's single sign-on (track P M5)
  help                   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

#### `cetra admin reapply-deletions`

```text
Re-open the deletions of another data directory that this one lacks (after a backup restore). Both `meta.db` files must be at this binary's schema; run `cetra admin migrate` on a restored older backup first

Usage: cetra admin reapply-deletions [OPTIONS] --from <FROM>

Options:
      --from <FROM>
          The data directory whose `meta.db` holds the deletions to re-apply (for example the directory as it was before the restore)

      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Overrides `CETRA_CONFIG`

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

#### `cetra admin backup`

```text
Back up the running server into DIR (online; the server writes DIR)

Usage: cetra admin backup [OPTIONS] --to <TO>

Options:
      --to <TO>
          Target directory on the server's filesystem: absent or empty, outside the data directory

      --meta-only
          Metadata only (S3-compatible object storage; objects stay in the bucket)

      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Overrides `CETRA_CONFIG`

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

#### `cetra admin gc-orphans`

```text
Delete objects the catalog does not know and report the ones it misses. Stop the server first

Usage: cetra admin gc-orphans [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --min-age <MIN_AGE>
          Leave unknown objects younger than this (e.g. `1h`, `30m`)
          
          [default: 1h]

      --dry-run
          Report only; delete nothing

      --rollback-bucket
          Required in S3 mode without `--dry-run`: deleting orphans there rolls the live bucket back

      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Overrides `CETRA_CONFIG`

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### `cetra login`

```text
Save a personal access token for a server.

The token expires after 90 days. Run `cetra login` again when it does.

Usage: cetra login [OPTIONS] --url <URL>

Options:
      --url <URL>
          Server URL, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8080`

      --no-browser
          Print the login URL and do not open a browser

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `cetra logout`

```text
Revoke the saved personal access token

Usage: cetra logout [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --url <URL>
          Server URL. Required when more than one server is saved

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### `cetra query`

```text
Run a SQL query on a project

Usage: cetra query [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> [SQL]

Arguments:
  [SQL]
          The SQL statement, with optional {name:Type} parameters. Put `--` before a statement that starts with `-`

Options:
      --file <PATH>
          Read the statement from a file; `-` reads stdin

      --project <PROJECT>
          Project UUID or org-slug/project-slug
          
          [env: CETRA_PROJECT=]

      --param <NAME=VALUE>
          A parameter value; repeat for each parameter. Int and Timestamp values that are all digits are sent as integers (Timestamp: epoch milliseconds)

      --from <TIME>
          Window start, RFC 3339. Needs --to

      --to <TIME>
          Window end (exclusive), RFC 3339. Needs --from

      --since <DURATION>
          Window ending now, for example 30m, 24h or 7d

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Most rows for table and json (1–10000). The server's default is 10000

      --timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>
          The server's query time limit in milliseconds (1000–60000). Its default is 60000

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - table:   Aligned columns
          - json:    A JSON array of row objects, pretty-printed
          - csv:     CSV export, streamed
          - ndjson:  One JSON object per line, streamed
          - parquet: Parquet export, streamed
          
          [default: table]

  -o, --output <PATH>
          Write the output to this file instead of stdout

      --url <URL>
          Server URL. Defaults to the only server saved by `cetra login`
          
          [env: CETRA_URL=]

      --token <TOKEN>
          Personal access token. Defaults to the token `cetra login` saved for the server. A value given as a flag is visible to other local users in the process list; prefer CETRA_TOKEN or `cetra login`
          
          [env: CETRA_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

### `cetra traces`

```text
List and show traces

Usage: cetra traces <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list  List traces, newest first by default
  get   Show one trace as a span tree
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

#### `cetra traces list`

```text
List traces, newest first by default

Usage: cetra traces list [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT>

Options:
      --project <PROJECT>
          Project UUID or org-slug/project-slug
          
          [env: CETRA_PROJECT=]

      --filter <DSL>
          Filter DSL over the traces view (spec 05), for example "status = 'error'"

      --search <TEXT>
          Full-text search over span input, output, name and system instructions

      --from <TIME>
          Range start: RFC 3339 or epoch milliseconds

      --to <TIME>
          Range end (exclusive): RFC 3339 or epoch milliseconds

      --since <DURATION>
          Range ending now, for example 30m, 24h or 7d

      --sort <SORT>
          Sort key

          Possible values:
          - start_time:   Earliest span start
          - duration:     Trace duration
          - cost_total:   Total cost
          - total_tokens: Total tokens
          
          [default: start_time]

      --order <ORDER>
          Sort direction

          Possible values:
          - asc:  Smallest or earliest first
          - desc: Largest or latest first
          
          [default: desc]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Traces per page (1–1000)
          
          [default: 50]

      --cursor <CURSOR>
          Cursor printed by the previous page

      --include-eval
          Include traces of the evaluation environment

      --include-experiments
          Include experiment traces

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - table: Aligned columns
          - json:  The server's JSON, re-indented
          
          [default: table]

      --url <URL>
          Server URL. Defaults to the only server saved by `cetra login`
          
          [env: CETRA_URL=]

      --token <TOKEN>
          Personal access token. Defaults to the token `cetra login` saved for the server. A value given as a flag is visible to other local users in the process list; prefer CETRA_TOKEN or `cetra login`
          
          [env: CETRA_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

#### `cetra traces get`

```text
Show one trace as a span tree

Usage: cetra traces get [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> <TRACE_ID>

Arguments:
  <TRACE_ID>
          Trace id, 32 hex digits

Options:
      --project <PROJECT>
          Project UUID or org-slug/project-slug
          
          [env: CETRA_PROJECT=]

      --around <TIME>
          When the trace happened, RFC 3339 or epoch milliseconds; speeds up the lookup

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - tree: One line per span, indented by depth
          - json: The server's JSON, re-indented
          
          [default: tree]

      --url <URL>
          Server URL. Defaults to the only server saved by `cetra login`
          
          [env: CETRA_URL=]

      --token <TOKEN>
          Personal access token. Defaults to the token `cetra login` saved for the server. A value given as a flag is visible to other local users in the process list; prefer CETRA_TOKEN or `cetra login`
          
          [env: CETRA_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
